anomalies.observed: Closing one SW6 pole connects /CAN0_N through R34 (120Ω) to /CAN1_N through R35 (120Ω). Closing the other pole directly connects /CAN0_P to /CAN1_P. Thus the switches can couple the two CAN channels rather than terminate each channel across its own P/N pair.
anomalies.expected: CAN0 and CAN1 should remain separate buses, as specified. If SW6 is for selectable termination, each enabled 120Ω termination should connect across the corresponding bus's own P and N lines, not between the two buses.

evidence.quote: two isolated CAN buses (CAN0, CAN1), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller

anomalies.impact: When the switch poles are closed, the CAN channels are no longer electrically independent; this can cause bus interference and prevents the switches from providing proper per-bus differential termination.

parsed.summary: SW6's wiring can couple the CAN0 and CAN1 signal pairs instead of providing separate, correctly placed CAN terminations. This conflicts with the specified independent CAN buses.
